title: Trace the checkout
description: Follow validation, storage, and the confirmation response.
learningObjectives: Trace a checkout across three modules

steps.title: Reject an empty cart
steps.narration: The checkout handler receives the cart and rejects an empty list before creating an order. This establishes the caller's first validation boundary.

steps.title: Validate quantities
steps.narration: The application boundary checks every quantity for a positive integer before handing the cart to storage. An invalid quantity throws an error back to the caller.

steps.title: Save the record
steps.narration: The store copies the cart items into a new order with an identifier and timestamp. This example uses an in-memory map, so orders do not survive a process restart.

steps.title: Return the confirmation
steps.narration: The order identifier travels back to checkout, which returns a confirmation message. The caller depends on the order boundary rather than knowing how the order is stored.

recap: Checkout validates an empty cart, the application boundary checks quantities, storage saves an in-memory order, and the identifier returns to the caller.
